Summary: Simplified multi-team delivery for a new or rebuilt Blazor SSR, WASM, or WASM PWA application from project-structure requirements.
ValueStatement: Agents build the requested Blazor app and prove it with build, test, browser screenshots, console checks, cleanup, summaries, and project-structure evidence.
InterfaceContractSummary: Generic Blazor SSR, WASM, and WASM PWA work is driven by project-structure source-of-truth data, process artifacts, and agent tool contracts.
GovernanceNotes: The process core remains generic. Blazor app specifics live in this template, step instructions, agent skills/tools, and project-structure records.
ChangeSummary: Adds a reusable generic Blazor process with required build, test, runtime, browser screenshot, console, cleanup, summary, and project-structure evidence contracts.
GovernancePolicySummary: Do not close until build/test proof, runtime/browser proof, screenshots, console status, cleanup, and project-structure writeback are present or a blocker is classified.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Agents own delivery and validation; Codex/user observation may approve or reject process escalations but must not manually build the app.
OperatingModeSummary: Governed live execution for local Blazor application delivery.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Suitable for demo and development Blazor runs using PostgreSQL-backed CanDoItAll runtime data.
Metrics: Runs with complete screenshot and console evidence.
Repair cycles caused by missing proof versus product defects.
Risks: Agents produce chat-only proof instead of process-visible screenshots.
Agents run the wrong project root or app mode.
Agents skip console inspection and miss JavaScript runtime errors.
Evidence is not written back to project structure.
TailoringRules: Use the project-structure declared Blazor mode; do not switch SSR/WASM/PWA without a decision record.
For visible UI surfaces, browser screenshots and console evidence are mandatory.
For backend-only work, API/runtime proof is mandatory and browser proof is required when a visible verification route exists.
Output folders must stay under the approved run folder.

Steps.Subtitle: Project structure and output root
Steps.Notes: Read project structure and run prompt. Resolve Blazor mode (SSR, WASM, or WASM PWA), product root, output root under C:\programovani\dotnet-demo\output or requested equivalent, run folder, acceptance criteria, routes/screens, backend/API expectations, exclusions, and required evidence writeback targets. Keep the app description generic and do not add sample-specific assumptions.

Steps.Title: Build Blazor application
Steps.Subtitle: Build-capable implementation
Steps.Notes: Create or update the requested Blazor solution and app using the project-structure declared mode, package choices, routes, features, and output folder. Use workspace file and command tools only inside the approved product root. Run dotnet restore before build-sensitive changes when dependencies changed. Run dotnet build after implementation. Do not mark complete if explicit acceptance criteria are omitted, if output is written outside the approved run folder, or if project-structure constraints are narrowed without a decision record.

Steps.Title: Validate Blazor runtime and browser evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Build/test/browser proof
Steps.Notes: Run validation against the delivered Blazor SSR, WASM, or WASM PWA app. Run dotnet restore, dotnet build, and dotnet test when a test project exists or was created. Start the app once from the approved product root and record the startup receipt. Use Playwright browser tools for every visible UI surface named by project structure or implementation evidence. Capture screenshot image paths, browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, browser_console_messages output, actual URL or entrypoint, visible behavior assertions, and cleanup receipt. For new app delivery, include the matching API/backend proof as well. Missing, blank, detached, stale, or chat-only screenshots are not acceptable.

Steps.Title: Record Blazor results and evidence index
Steps.Subtitle: Project structure writeback
Steps.Notes: Write a compact run evidence index, agent self-review summary, output-root path, screenshot references, console status, build/test status, and final verdict back into project structure through APIs/tools. Before completing, use project_structure_asset_create for screenshot or evidence files that must become project assets, and use project_structure_node_create to attach the final verdict and evidence index to the target work item. Include concrete node ids, asset ids, and raw record pointers only where needed for selective follow-up. If these project-structure tool calls cannot be completed, return status Blocked with the failed tool names and do not select the Error branch as a completed outcome.

Steps.Title: Escalate unresolved Blazor repair findings
Steps.Subtitle: No-go repair escalation
Steps.Notes: Capture unresolved post-repair findings and make the Blazor delivery no-go or replan decision explicit instead of silently closing the process.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Post-repair Blazor validation evidence, repair notes, and remaining product or proof-blocking findings.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit no-go, scope reset, or replan decision with accountable owner and required next repair scope.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Escalation decision, unresolved defect/proof-gap list, failed URLs or APIs, screenshot/console references when available, and owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Blazor delivery manager owns escalation and cannot treat unresolved repair evidence as delivery-ready.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not record successful delivery while post-repair validation remains unresolved. Artifact recovery: block when missing artifact materialization, invalid required artifact evidence, or process-visible proof gaps are detected.
